pr_title: Fix ß bug in regexp for mentions and tags
pr_comments: LOL, ß is the nemesis 😆

I somehow feel like there may be a bug hidden here, because the issues only happen:
- for `ß` (and not German special characters in general or non-ASCII characters or anything like that). I somehow have the gut feeling that it's related to the fact that `ß` doesn't have the lowercase or uppercase version or something like that
- when the case insensitive mode is enabled for a regex
- when negative lookbehind is used (https://ruby-doc.org/3.2.2/Regexp.html#class-Regexp-label-Anchors)

As if too many negations were causing a subtle bug in Ruby regex logic.

However, I gave up on trying to find a minimum reproduction example which clearly shows the bug, and disabled the case insensitive mode where it's not needed.
You might want to reopen this PR with a branch without the special character in the branch name: Perhaps `fix/eszett-before-mentions-and-hashtags-breaking`

Also, it'd be really good to add tests for a wider array of unicode characters before mentions and hashtags, perhaps you can do a fuzzing test with `#{Faker::String.random(length: 4)} @alice@foo.example` and `#{Faker::String.random(length: 4)} #example`

> I somehow feel like there may be a bug hidden here

I have got a feeling this is related to https://bugs.ruby-lang.org/issues/4044, a bug report that is linked from the `Regexp` documentation.

issue_context.title: Mentioned handles are rendered as plaintext without link if the sharp s ('ß') character appears in the previous word
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce the problem

1. Write a post with the following content and send it

`Gemäß @Gargron@mastodon.social`

### Expected behaviour

The handle is rendered with a link to the profile: Gemäß @Gargron

### Actual behaviour

The handle is rendered as plaintext: Gemäß @Gargron@mastodon.social

### Detailed description

Apparently when a handle is mentioned after a "ß" (sharp s) character it is always rendered as plaintext.

Please find the following post where it was first observed:
https://nrw.social/@melsdung/112784007422571926

The issue could also be reproduced with the 3rd party app "Tusky" using mastodon.online.

### Mastodon instance

mastodon.online and nrw.social

### Mastodon version

v4.2.10 (nrw.social) and v4.3.0-nightly.2024-07-11 (mastodon.online)

### Technical details

If this is happening on your own Mastodon server, please fill out those:
- Ruby version: (from `ruby --version`, eg. v3.1.2)
- Node.js version: (from `node --version`, eg. v18.16.0)
comments: Interesting bug. It only happens when `ß` is the last character before the handle. It also doesn't happen to other special characters in German (for example `ä`) The same happens to tags

review_comments: I believe that we don't need the case insensitive mode here, because the regexp is constructed from character classes that capture both lower and upper case.
I added this test to make sure that the case insensitive matching is working correctly. This test passes on `main`.
I really like this idea. Would you mind adding the same for hashtags?

The cases insensitive mode (`i`) is not needed here, because it's enabled for `USERNAME_RE`. According to the documentation (https://ruby-doc.org/3.2.2/Regexp.html#class-Regexp-label-Options)

> i, m, and x can also be applied on the subexpression level with the (?on-off) construct, which enables options on, and disables options off for the expression enclosed by the parentheses

And this magically works when including one regexp in another 🎉
